title: a reseal that cannot run raises a trouble, and the commit still lands
intention: A pre-commit reseal that crashes raises a trouble carrying the error, and the commit still lands.
why: Measured 2026-11-12: a full /tmp crashed cairn test --reseal --stage at tester/cli.py:712 inside the pre-commit hook; the hook's || true swallowed it and the commit landed rc 0 with no seals staged and nothing recorded.
traces_to: Law 7 (an error is permanent in a record of truth) and the 2026-09-30 ruling that the hook never blocks.
how: reseal.run_or_record(run, *, raiser=None, standing=None) runs the ladder; on an Exception it prints the traceback, raises trouble tester-reseal-could-not-run (error, message, traceback tail) and returns 3; on completion it clears that trouble if it stands. cli._reseal_run wraps the renamed _reseal_ladder through it. KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit pass through. The hook is unchanged.

clauses.claim: a run raising OSError(ENOSPC) returns 3 and raises exactly one trouble under tester-reseal-could-not-run, carrying the error and the traceback tail
a run that completes returns its own code and clears that trouble only when it stands
a KeyboardInterrupt passes through and raises nothing
cli._reseal_run goes through the door (a staged-file read failing with ENOSPC yields 3 and the trouble), and the hook still runs the reseal under || true and exits 0

decisions.text: D1: run_or_record and RUN_CRASH_IDENTITY join reseal.py above reseal_all, reusing _raise, CLEARS_FOR and CALLER.
D2: cli._reseal_run becomes a wrapper over the renamed _reseal_ladder through run_or_record.
D3: the proof holds one tooth per clause, fake raisers only.
